meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to mean'.

examples.trans: Pasha, what does all this mean?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'there, thither', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я знаю! Хочешь, сейчас и тебя туда увезут?
examples.trans: I know! Do you want them to take you there too right now?
They put bad meat in there for you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'бавлять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to add, supplement'.

examples.text: Я добавляю свежую зелень и соус.
examples.trans: I add fresh greens and sauce.

examples.text: Макс, быстрее! Уже пора добавлять яйца.
examples.trans: Max, faster! It is time to add the eggs.
Add the dye slowly and carefully.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'колько'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Common masculine noun meaning 'year' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I've been working here for four years.

examples.text: Это было давно, тридцать лет назад.
examples.trans: That was long ago, thirty years back.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'our, ours', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common masculine noun meaning 'guest, visitor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, к вам гости! Па-пам!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, you have visitors! Ta-da!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'well; come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'about', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to think', paired with 'подумать'.

examples.trans: I have no time to think about that.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'they', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to sleep', paired with 'поспать'.

examples.text: Ладно, утром позвоню ей. Поехали спать.
examples.trans: All right, I'll call her in the morning. Let's go to sleep.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'могать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to help', paired with 'помочь'.

examples.text: Так, операцию продолжаем. Михаил Михайлович, помогайте Лаврову.
examples.trans: Right, the operation goes on. Mikhail Mikhailovich, give Lavrov your help.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how; as', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

получаться.gloss: to work out, to come out

meanings.en: to work out, to come out
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лучаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to work out, to come out', paired with 'получиться'.

examples.text: Нет, не получается у меня это забыть. Удачи тебе на новом месте работы.
examples.trans: No, I just can't forget it. Good luck to you in your new job.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'when', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: When I grow up, I'll be the mayor.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('ready').
High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'my, mine', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'алат'). Common masculine noun meaning 'salad' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Седьмой столик заказал салат с трюфелями.
examples.trans: Table seven ordered a salad with truffles.

examples.text: Гость пришёл специально ради этого салата.
examples.trans: The guest came especially for this salad.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

нервничать.gloss: to be nervous, get worked up

meanings.en: to be nervous, get worked up
meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'рвничать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be nervous, get worked up'.

examples.text: Павел Юрьевич, вам нельзя нервничать сейчас.
examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, you mustn't get worked up right now.
I am not getting worked up!

examples.text: Я не нервничаю! Рейтинг Самсонова сравнялся с нашим?
examples.trans: I'm not getting worked up! Has Samsonov's rating drawn level with ours?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in (time); through', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нормально? Она через неделю снова потечёт!
examples.trans: Fine? It'll be leaking again in a week!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'seven', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Там депозит на семь тысяч рублей!
examples.trans: There's a deposit for seven thousand roubles!

examples.text: Семь тысяч, давай сходим! Ты же любишь морепродукты.
examples.trans: Seven thousand, let's go! After all, you love seafood.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'minute' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll be there in ten minutes.

examples.text: Ладно, будь там. Через десять минут буду.
examples.trans: All right, stay there. I'll be there in ten minutes.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?
